Rashi on Gittin 56b:11:1.hebrew: כמין גרגותני - סל גדול ששופים בו יין מגת לבור, וקורין קולדויי"ר:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:11:1.english: Like a gargutni - a large basket through which they pour wine from the winepress into the vat, and they call [it] coledoir [in Old French]:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:11:2.english: And they were forgotten [i.e., praised] in the city where they had so done - [saying, "Behold] this mighty deed that you see!":

Rashi on Gittin 56b:12:1.english: Things that are hidden - [this refers to] the hidden treasure of Israel's wealth:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:13:2.english: Sisera - [As the verse states:] "The brook Kishon swept them away" [Judges 5:21]:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:14:1.english: An entrance - a mouth to take in food:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:14:2.english: An exit - an outlet via the rectum:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:15:2.english: It became silent - that gnat [stopped] pecking because of the sound of the hammer:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:15:3.hebrew: כיון דדש דש - משהרגיל היתוש ולמד בקול הקורנס, הכיר בו ולא הניח ניקורו:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:15:3.english: Since it became accustomed, it became accustomed - Once the gnat became accustomed to and learned the sound of the hammer, it recognized it and did not cease its pecking:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:1:1.english: In truth, you are a king - You are destined to be a king:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:1:2.english: And their mighty one shall be of themselves, and their ruler shall proceed from the midst of them - Thus, "mighty one" is "ruler":

Rashi on Gittin 56b:1:3.english: Lebanon is the Temple - because it whitens [i.e., cleanses] the iniquities of Israel:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:2:1.english: Wrapped around it - Attached [to it] and eager for it:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:2:2.hebrew: אין שוברין את החבית - כדי שילך לו הדרקון? כך היה לכם להשחית חומת העיר ולשורפה באש, כדי להשליך אותן בריוני מתוכה:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:2:2.english: [Do] they not break the barrel - so that the snake will go away? So too, you should have destroyed the city wall and burned it with fire, in order to cast those zealots out of it:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:2:3.hebrew: וחביתא שבקינן לה - כך היינו מצפים, אולי נוכל להם ולהוציאם ממנה, ותהיה העיר קיימת ונשלים עמך:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:2:3.english: And we leave the barrel - So [too] we were hoping: perhaps we could prevail over them [the rebels] and drive them out of it [the city], and the city would remain intact and we would make peace with you.

Rashi on Gittin 56b:3:2.english: It would not come off - because his limbs swelled from the joy of the news:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:4:1.hebrew: ורוח נכאה תיבש גרם - וכאשר תכאה רוחך מחמת השונא, תיבש העצם שלך:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:4:1.english: And a broken spirit dries the bones - And when your spirit is broken because of the enemy, your bone will dry up.

Rashi on Gittin 56b:5:1.english: Give me Yavneh - [meaning] that you should not destroy it and you should not kill its Sages.

Rashi on Gittin 56b:5:2.hebrew: ושושילתא דרבן גמליאל - משפחת הנשיא, שלא תהרגם, שלא תכלה שולטנות בית דוד:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:5:2.english: And the dynasty of Rabban Gamliel - [This refers to] the family of the Nasi, that you should not kill them, so that the rulership of the House of David will not cease:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:5:3.hebrew: ואסוותא - רופאים, תן לי מאנשיך שירפאו את רבי צדוק, שלא היה יכול לבלוע אוכל, לפי שנתקצרו מעיו בתעניותיו:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:5:3.english: And doctors - Doctors — give me [some] of your men to heal Rabbi Tzadok, who was unable to swallow food because his intestines had shrunk from his fasts.

Rashi on Gittin 56b:6:1.english: And he maintained - Rabban Yochanan maintained:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:6:2.hebrew: כולי האי - דלישבק לירושלים, לא עביד ליה, ואשתכח דאפי' הצלה פורתא לא עבדי; הלכך בעינא מיניה הא, דתיהוי הצלה פורתא:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:6:2.english: That much - [namely,] that he should spare Jerusalem, he would not do it, and it would turn out that even a small salvation would not be achieved; therefore, I will ask of him this [modest request], so that there will be a small salvation:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:7:1.english: Water of parei - Water in which bran was soaked:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:7:2.english: Water of sipuka - Coarse bran with flour mixed into it:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:9:1.english: Your enemies roar in the midst of Your meeting place - in the house in which You meet [with Israel]:

Rashi on Gittin 56b:9:2.hebrew: שמו אותותם אותות - אמרו שסימניהון סימן: דם זה של מי הוא, אם לא שהרגנו את עצמו:
Rashi on Gittin 56b:9:2.english: They have set up their own signs for signs - They said that their signs [i.e., the blood on the curtain] are a sign [of victory]: "Whose blood is this, if not that we have killed Himself [a euphemism for God]?"

Tosafot on Gittin 56b:15:1.hebrew: וניקר במוחו ז' שנים - לא נעשה טרפה בכך, דדרך חוטמו נכנס ולא ניקב הקרום; ועוד יש חילוק בין טריפות דאדם לבהמה, כדפרישית בפרק קמא דערובין (דף ז.):
Tosafot on Gittin 56b:15:1.english: And picked at his brain for seven years - He did not become a tereifah through this, for it entered through his nostril and the membrane [of the brain] was not punctured; and furthermore, there is a distinction between the tereifot of a human and [those of] an animal, as I explained in the first chapter of Eruvin (7a):

Tosafot on Gittin 56b:1:1.hebrew: אי לאו דמלכא את לא מימסרא ירושלים בידך - אע"ג דאכתי לא מימסרא בידו עד שבא טיטוס, מ"מ כיון דכבר צר עליה שלש שנים והוה כפנא, הוי כאילו כבר נמסרה:
Tosafot on Gittin 56b:1:1.english: If you are not a king, Jerusalem will not be handed over into your hand - Even though it had not yet been handed over into his hand until Titus came, nevertheless, since he had already besieged it for three years and there was a famine, it was as if it had already been handed over:

Tosafot on Gittin 56b:9:1.english: And a miracle was performed and there was blood, etc. - [This was] to make known that the destruction of the Temple is grievous before the Omnipresent:
